cases.sentence: Ты Манфред, ты ___, а мы как плевки у тебя под ногами.
cases.translation: You are Manfred, you are Cain, and we are like the spittle under your feet.
cases.explain: The word is a predicate joined to the subject «ты» with a zero copula (есть), and such predicate nouns stand in the nominative.

cases.sentence: И все это было сказано без ___, тоном до смерти оскорбленных.
cases.translation: And all this was said without a smile, in the tone of people mortally offended.
cases.explain: The preposition «без» ('without') always governs the genitive: без улыбки.

cases.sentence: Меня подводят к ___ и представляют так.
cases.translation: They lead me up to the ladies and introduce me like this.
cases.explain: «К» meaning motion towards a person takes the dative, so the plural дамы becomes дамам.

cases.translation: Drop all that about Ivan Turgenev.
cases.explain: «Про» ('about') governs the accusative; Тургенев is an animate masculine noun, so its accusative is identical to the genitive form.

cases.sentence: Они своими угрюмыми ___ пронзали мне душу.
cases.translation: With their gloomy stares they pierced my soul.
cases.explain: The means or instrument by which an action is done goes into the instrumental with no preposition: пронзали взглядами.

cases.translation: In this world there are certain things.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location rather than direction) requires the prepositional: в мире.

cases.translation: I know many of God's designs.
cases.explain: A noun that says whose something is ('God's designs') stands in the possessive genitive after the head noun замыслы.

reading.ru: До ветру ты не ходишь – вот что.
reading.question: What do Venichka's flatmates accuse him of?
options: That he never goes out to relieve himself
That he drinks up all their beer
That he never washes the dishes
That he comes home late every night
reading.correct: That he never goes out to relieve himself
reading.explain: Their whole grievance is that since he moved in they have never once seen him go to the toilet.

reading.question: What do the flatmates say happened as soon as Venichka moved in with them?
options: They immediately sensed that something was wrong
They immediately decided to throw him out
They immediately stopped talking to him
reading.correct: They immediately sensed that something was wrong
reading.explain: They claim they felt at once that something was not right, and then worked out what it was.

reading.ru: И все это было сказано без улыбки, тоном до смерти оскорбленных.
reading.question: In what manner was the accusation delivered?
options: Without a smile, in the tone of the mortally offended
As a friendly joke over beer
In a whisper, so the neighbours would not hear
With laughter and slaps on the back
reading.correct: Without a smile, in the tone of the mortally offended
reading.explain: The narrator stresses that there was no joking in it: they spoke as people deeply insulted.

reading.ru: Ты Манфред, ты Каин, а мы как плевки у тебя под ногами…
reading.question: According to the flatmates, how does Venichka's behaviour make them look?
options: Like spittle under the feet of a Cain and a Manfred
Like his equals in every way
Like guests in their own room
reading.correct: Like spittle under the feet of a Cain and a Manfred
reading.explain: They say that by refusing to do what they do he casts himself as Cain and Manfred and them as spittle underfoot.

reading.ru: Они, все четверо, глядели на меня уничтожающе.
reading.question: How many flatmates were staring Venichka down?
reading.explain: The narrator says all four of them looked at him witheringly, and he gave up arguing.

reading.question: How much beer does Venichka admit to having drunk that day?
options: Two large mugs and one small one
reading.correct: Two large mugs and one small one
reading.explain: This admission is what the flatmates use to prove that he must have to go.

reading.question: Why does Venichka finally get up and go?
options: To relieve them rather than himself
Because he could not hold out any longer
Because they threatened to throw him out
To fetch more beer for everyone
reading.correct: To relieve them rather than himself
reading.explain: He states that he went not to relieve himself but to relieve the others of their offence.

reading.ru: Я знаю многие замыслы Бога, но для чего Он вложил в меня столько целомудрия, я до сих пор так и не понял.
reading.question: What does Venichka say he still has not understood?
options: Why God put so much chastity into him
Why he keeps missing his train
Why he was hired as a brigade leader
reading.correct: Why God put so much chastity into him
reading.explain: He claims to know many of God's designs, but not the purpose of the modesty God gave him.

reading.ru: Я не могу при дамах не конфузиться.
reading.question: What does Venichka say always happens to him in the company of ladies?
options: He falls silent out of contempt
reading.explain: Introduced to the ladies at Pavlovo-Posad, he says he is incapable of not getting flustered in front of them.

reading.ru: Все наше московское управление сотрясается от ужаса, стоит им вспомнить об этих графиках.
reading.question: How does the Moscow office react to any mention of the individual work graphs?
options: The whole administration shudders with horror
The whole administration bursts out laughing
The administration asks him to explain them again
Nobody there remembers them any more
reading.correct: The whole administration shudders with horror
reading.explain: He introduces the story of his dismissal by saying the entire Moscow management shakes with horror at the memory of the graphs.

reading.ru: Мы чешем без остановки через Кусково!
reading.question: What is the train doing at Kuskovo?
options: Standing at the platform for a long time
reading.explain: Venichka notices where they are and remarks that they are hurtling through Kuskovo without a stop.

highlight.question: Which sentence says what the flatmates felt as soon as Venichka moved in with them?
sentences: До ветру ты не ходишь – вот что.
С тех пор как ты поселился, мы никто ни разу не видели, чтобы ты в туалет пошел.
Ну, ладно, по большой нужде еще ладно!
Но ведь ни разу даже по малой… даже по малой!
highlight.explain: The third sentence reports their immediate feeling that something was wrong, before they say what it was.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the real reason Venichka got up and went?
sentences: Ну что ж, я встал и пошел.
Не для того, чтобы облегчить себя.
А когда вернулся, один из них мне сказал: «С такими позорными взглядами ты вечно будешь одиноким и несчастным».
highlight.explain: The second sentence rules out his own comfort and the third names the true motive: relieving the others.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Venichka still cannot understand why God gave him so much chastity?
sentences: Я знаю многие замыслы Бога, но для чего Он вложил в меня столько целомудрия, я до сих пор так и не понял.
А это целомудрие – самое смешное! – это целомудрие толковалось так навыворот, что мне отказывали даже в самой элементарной воспитанности…
highlight.explain: The third sentence contrasts what he does know of God's designs with the one thing he does not.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the one recent episode Venichka has chosen to tell?
sentences: Я многое мог бы рассказать по этому предмету, но если я буду рассказывать все – я растяну до самых Петушков.

А лучше я не буду рассказывать все, а только один-единственный случай, потому что он самый свежий: о том, как неделю тому назад меня сняли с бригадирского поста за «внедрение порочной системы индивидуальных графиков».
Все наше московское управление сотрясается от ужаса, стоит им вспомнить об этих графиках.
А чего же тут ужасного, казалось бы!
highlight.explain: The second sentence announces the single story he will tell: his removal from the brigade leader's post a week earlier.
